summary_html: Agency fails to **disclose required data or reports**, obstructing transparency. Federal statutes require public reporting under CAPTA, FOIA, and Sunshine provisions.
authority_html:

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Basey v. State, Department of Public Safety, Division of Alaska State Troopers
key_cases.holding: The State failed to establish either the AS 40.25.122 litigation exception or the law-enforcement exception to the Alaska Public Records Act, so dismissal of the records requester's suit was error and the case was remanded.
key_cases.relevance: Places the burden on the State to justify each claimed exemption before it may withhold public records.
key_cases.quote: We conclude it was error for the superior court to grant the State's motion to dismiss pursuant to AS 40.25.122.

key_cases.case_name: Rowan B. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Civil discovery rules, not the Public Records Act exemptions, govern a CINA parent's request for law-enforcement records, and the trial court erred by denying the request outright instead of conducting an in camera review.
key_cases.relevance: Rejects agency reliance on Public Records Act exemptions as a basis for withholding records from a party litigant.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the trial court erred in denying Rowan access to materials he sought through discovery without at least conducting an in camera review.

key_cases.case_name: Simone H. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: The trial court acted within its discretion in refusing to release the child's therapy records to the mother for use at the termination trial, and substantial evidence supported the finding that OCS made reasonable efforts to reunify the family.
key_cases.relevance: Marks the limit on disclosure: a child's therapy records may be withheld even from a parent facing termination.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the trial court acted within its discretion in denying Simone's request for access to Irving's therapy records

key_cases.case_name: Jacob v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Grandparents were entitled to a declaratory judgment that OCS violated their statutory rights to notice of and participation in their grandchildren's CINA proceedings, but their remaining claims — including the request for systemic injunctive relief — became moot once they intervened.
key_cases.relevance: Declares OCS's failure to provide statutorily required notice unlawful.
key_cases.quote: We hold that all other issues are moot due to the Jacobs' subsequent intervention in their grandchildren's CINA proceedings.
